implementation_notes: Default modern realization: an unordered_map held in a function-local static, reached through a free accessor function, with register/make free functions built on it. It replaces the hand-written Registry class (and avoids header-order coupling) with two functions and the STL container.
pitfalls: Concurrent register and lookup are not safe: unordered_map has no internal locking, so either restrict registration to start-up or add std::shared_mutex with a unique_lock for writers.

Self-registering translation units can be discarded by the linker in static libraries (nothing references them), so the registry looks empty - the construct-on-first-use accessor fixes initialization order, not inclusion.

Entries live until exit (destruction order of function-local statics is reverse construction order), and every erased value must still be type-correct at the point of std::any_cast or it throws bad_any_cast.

variants.name: std::any type-erased registry
variants.implementation_notes: When entries are heterogeneous (any registered object, not just one factory signature), store std::any in the map and downcast at lookup: the registry becomes a process-wide key/value store while registration and lookup stay type-checked only at the cast site. Prefer the homogeneous map whenever a single interface suffices.
pitfalls: std::any requires C++17 and stores a copy (or a pointer) of the value: registering a non-copyable type only works through a pointer/smart pointer.
Insertion overwrites silently with insert_or_assign; a duplicate-registration policy has to be built on top (emplace + .second, or a check).
Lookup type errors are runtime exceptions, so the registry cannot give the compile-time safety a checked factory map provides.

variants.name: constinit self-registering table
variants.implementation_notes: C++20 answer to the initialization-order problem: a static constexpr-capable container declared constinit is constant-initialized before any dynamic initializer runs, so classes can register themselves with a static bool member without depending on translation-unit order. Choose it when the registry must exist before main() (test discovery, plugin tables) and the table fits a fixed capacity.
pitfalls: constinit only guarantees constant initialization of the container itself; the registering static bool in another translation unit is still dynamically initialized, so the table must tolerate any insertion order.

std::unordered_map/std::map are not usable in constant expressions - the table must be a fixed-capacity std::array or a custom constexpr map, which caps entry count and forbids duplicates only by explicit check.
Registrations still disappear when the linker drops the translation unit, and the constinit declaration is a compile-time error if anything in the initializer is not constexpr-constructible.
